Exercise 3: tapply and sapply

Name: William Gottschalk

Date: November 5, 2026

Load state data

data(state)

this data is stored in a slightly different way than other datasets we’ve used so far

run this line of code to avoid later confusion

states = as.data.frame(state.x77)

1: What is the average population, income, and area of all 50 states ins the states dataset?

Your code here:

apply(states[, c("Population", "Income", "Area")], 2, mean)
## Population     Income       Area 
##    4246.42    4435.80   70735.88

2. What is the average area of the states from different regions of the country?

Hint: use the object state.region in your environment

Your code here:

tapply(states$Area, state.region, mean)
##     Northeast         South North Central          West 
##      18141.00      54605.12      62652.00     134463.00

4. Let’s assume that we don’t want to live in a state with high illiteracy, high murder, and

many freezing days; also assume that each of these factors contribute equally to our opinion

(Illiteracy * Murder * Frost) = undesirable

What 10 states should we avoid? # hint use prod(); and maybe order()

Your code here:

undesirable <- apply(states[, c("Illiteracy", "Murder", "Frost")], 1, prod)
avoid <- order(undesirable, decreasing=TRUE)
names(undesirable)[head(avoid, 10)]
##  [1] "Alaska"         "New Mexico"     "South Carolina" "Georgia"       
##  [5] "Kentucky"       "North Carolina" "Mississippi"    "Tennessee"     
##  [9] "New York"       "Michigan"

#used apply() to apply prod function to the three rows of interest in the states data and put that into undesirable object #used order and decreasing to rank the undesirable outcome and put in avoid object #used names on the undesirable object before using head to look at first 10 states in avoid object

5. Use sapply() to plot a histogram of the data below 4 times, in 4 different colors.

For extra style, title the plot by it’s color, e.g. the red plot is titled “red”

Your code here:

sapply(c("red", "green", "blue", "orange"), function(color) hist(states$Murder, col = color, main = color, xlab = "Murders" ))

##          red             green           blue            orange         
## breaks   numeric,9       numeric,9       numeric,9       numeric,9      
## counts   integer,8       integer,8       integer,8       integer,8      
## density  numeric,8       numeric,8       numeric,8       numeric,8      
## mids     numeric,8       numeric,8       numeric,8       numeric,8      
## xname    "states$Murder" "states$Murder" "states$Murder" "states$Murder"
## equidist TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE

6. Standardize all the variables in the states dataset and save your answer to a new

dataframe, states_standardized

Hint: to standardize a variable, you subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation (sd)

Your code here:

states_standardized <- as.data.frame(sapply(states, function(x) (x-(mean(x))) / sd(x)))
head(states_standardized)

7. Create a histogram again for each variable in the states data, but this time label each

histogram with the variable names when you plot

Hint: instead of using apply to iterate over the columns themselves, you can often iterate

over the column names with sapply

Your code here:

sapply(names(states), function(col) hist(states[[col]], main = col, xlab = col))

##          Population      Income          Illiteracy      Life Exp       
## breaks   numeric,6       integer,8       numeric,6       integer,8      
## counts   integer,5       integer,7       integer,5       integer,7      
## density  numeric,5       numeric,7       numeric,5       numeric,7      
## mids     numeric,5       numeric,7       numeric,5       numeric,7      
## xname    "states[[col]]" "states[[col]]" "states[[col]]" "states[[col]]"
## equidist TRUE            TRUE            TRUE            TRUE           
##          Murder          HS Grad         Frost           Area           
## breaks   numeric,9       integer,8       numeric,11      numeric,7      
## counts   integer,8       integer,7       integer,10      integer,6      
## density  numeric,8       numeric,7       numeric,10      numeric,6      
## mids     numeric,8       numeric,7       numeric,10      numeric,6
